clue.text: Over-indulged pilots' mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of the word before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Airmen in their mess are pampered and spoilt by their hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the officers' dining room, but it signals an anagram of PILOTS; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pampered child given everything is said to be indulged to excess, the same sense.

clue.text: Break out without a point ahead in view

indicators.note: ahead puts the compass point in front of the rest

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for break out goes round the letter A

parts.note: to break out of prison is to escape

explanation.surface: A prisoner breaks out without any sharp tool ahead in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so ESCAPE wraps A to give EASCAPE, with S in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or picture of the sea is a type of view.

clue.text: Run or row against the wind

indicators.note: to wind something is to twist it, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: V stands for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Rowing or running into the wind is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' rhymes with 'kind' here, a twisting, not the breeze. In cricket an overthrow is an extra run scored when a fielder's throw goes past the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a ball thrown in by a fielder that escapes the wicket gives the batsmen an extra run.

clue.text: Positioned in pole a driver's to go in front

indicators.note: the answer's letters are positioned inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A racing driver on pole position will go out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' evokes pole position in motor racing, which fits the definition well.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the lead is to be at the front, ahead of everyone.

clue.text: Motorway rush hour for example

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Motorway rush hour for example (8)': M + SPRINT (rush) leaves an I that no clue word supplies, and no source for the printed clue was found; a word such as 'one' or 'I' seems lost.

clue.text: Fashion is art in a decorative facade

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of the words after are reshaped

explanation.surface: Fashion is presented as art in an ornamental front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' is a verb, to shape, not the clothing trade, though intarsia is also a knitting pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Intarsia is decorative inlaid woodwork or patterned knitting, an ornamental surface.

clue.text: Strange happenings relative to academy set on functioning regularly

definitions.note: an adjective in the answer standing for events beyond science, as in 'the paranormal'

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces are set on top of the last

parts.note: pa is a father, a relative
RA is the Royal Academy
normal means working as usual

explanation.surface: Strange events relate to a school set in its normal routine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'set on' puts PARA above NORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts and telepathy are events outside scientific explanation, the territory of the supernatural.

clue.text: Mode of expression that's the same on an island

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: id. is short for idem, Latin for the same
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Islanders share the same way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: ID. abbreviates Latin idem, the same; IOM is the Isle of Man, between England and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase whose meaning is fixed by usage is a turn of phrase, a way of putting things.

clue.text: Big bang more generally made by the jazz musician

parts.note: Kid Ory was a New Orleans jazz trombonist

explanation.surface: A jazz musician makes a big bang on the drums.
explanation.walkthrough: Big bang is the best-known cosmological theory; 'more generally' takes the definition from the example to the class.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Bang is one model of the universe's origin, an explanatory idea.

clue.text: Medium good oil supplier

parts.note: Esso is an oil and petrol brand

explanation.surface: A medium consults a good oil firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, but it is an artist's medium.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster and glue mixture used as a ground for painting and gilding is an artist's material.

clue.text: Sort of mean girl in teens say

indicators.note: the girl's name is placed inside the word for a time of life

parts.note: the teens are an example of an age of life
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A nasty teenage girl is described as a mean girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl' could be many names; the teens, being a stage of life, steer the solver to the right container.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the commonest kind of typical value, so the word names one sort of mean.

clue.text: Flier Lawrence initially held an order of merit

indicators.note: the initials hold the rearranged letters between them

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials T and E

indicators.note: an order here is an arrangement, so the letters of the following word are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia is honoured with the Order of Merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an order of merit' reads as the British honour (the Order of Merit), but 'an order of' signals that the letters of the last word are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Winged termites swarm through the air at mating time, so the insect can be called a flying creature.

clue.text: Musical tom tom

definitions.meaning: a long-running Lloyd Webber stage show based on T. S. Eliot's poems
a tom is a male cat, so two toms make several felines

explanation.surface: A drum is the subject: the tom-tom, a musical percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage show is named for felines, and two toms, male felines, are a plural of the animal.

clue.text: There's no star more moving for a stargazer

indicators.note: moving the letters around puts the three words into a new order

explanation.surface: No sight thrills a stargazer more than a moving star, a shooting one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' seems to describe a shooting star, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies the heavens through a telescope is literally one who gazes at the stars.

clue.text: Tormented having long lived wildly using ecstasy in bed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for bed
wildly signals the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A wild liver of the high life, high on drugs in bed, is tormented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges L and LIVED into DEVILL; the bed is split so the inner part sits after its first two letters. 'long lived wildly' reads as a hedonist's past.
explanation.definitionFit: To be plagued by troubles is to be harassed, as if by a devil.

clue.text: Whistler's financial manager?

parts.note: someone who whistles purses the lips, so one who does so might jokingly share a name with a ship's officer in charge of money

explanation.surface: The painter Whistler is imagined having an accountant to look after his affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital W points to the painter, but a whistler is anyone who puckers the lips, and the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the officer who keeps the accounts and handles passengers' money has this title.

clue.text: Chamber where the volume count is high though it's usually hushed

definitions.text: Chamber where the volume count is high though it's usually hushed

parts.words: Chamber where the volume count is high though it's usually hushed
parts.note: volume seems to mean loudness, which would clash with the hush, but here it means books, of which there are many

explanation.surface: A paradoxical room where the noise level is high yet everyone is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'volume' as loudness and the clue is a contradiction; read it as books and it is a quiet room full of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A room holding a large collection of books, where silence is the rule.

clue.text: Soldiers in tears turning to ecstasy to get lift again

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: turning reverses the word for tears

parts.note: tears here are rips, from tear as in torn
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Soldiers in tears turn to drugs to lift their spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' rhymes with 'bears': rips, which 'turning' reverses to SPIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire anew is to raise the spirits once more.

clue.text: Footballer put off going round goal

indicators.note: the word for postpone goes round the word for goal

parts.note: to put off is to defer
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer is put off by having to go round the goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' is END in the sense of an aim, not the net.
explanation.definitionFit: A player whose job is guarding his team's goal from attackers.

clue.text: Worker bit noble

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as a farm hand
some is a bit of something

explanation.surface: A worker becomes a bit of a noble.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean generous and fine, as in a handsome gesture.

clue.text: Back brush

definitions.meaning: in football, a defender who plays behind the other backs
a broom used to clear floors or chimneys

explanation.surface: A two-word picture of someone brushing their back.
explanation.definitionFit: A football defender who sweeps up behind the back line, and a tool for sweeping floors, share the name.

clue.text: Airman all at sea in the dock

indicators.note: being all at sea is being confused, so the letters of the word before are muddled

explanation.surface: A pilot finds himself floundering in the water by the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all at sea' fits the nautical scene, yet it signals an anagram of AIRMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour basin with moorings for yachts and pleasure boats is a kind of dock.

clue.text: Second runabout — a black beetle!

parts.note: a runabout is a small car
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: A second little black car darts about like a beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: The VW Beetle makes 'runabout' and 'beetle' a neat car picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred dung beetle of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Short report written up as metaphor

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means read from bottom to top
short means a letter is cut from the word, here its first

explanation.surface: A short report is written up as a metaphor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops R from REPORT, leaving EPORT; 'written up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, of which metaphor is an example.

clue.text: Back issue in market giving short measure

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the word for a market

parts.note: a market or shopping centre

indicators.note: back means the word for issue is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to issue is to emit or send out

explanation.surface: An old magazine issue in a market is sold with less than its full weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the word for issue. 'short measure' sounds like cheating customers but simply means a small unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of a metre is a small unit of length.

clue.text: Quintessential Englishman in a different vein to Newton

indicators.note: different means the letters of the word are made into a different order

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: An Englishman compared with Isaac Newton, in a different vein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newton' suggests Isaac Newton, but it is N, the unit's symbol. David NIVEN was the actor who epitomised the suave Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor David Niven was famous for playing debonair British gentlemen.

clue.text: It's exploited and a little bemused

indicators.note: a little of the word means only part of its letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone who has been taken advantage of is left a bit bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' sounds like 'slightly', but it means a small part of BEMUSED is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploited and taken advantage of are the same idea: something put to work for another's gain.

clue.text: Jazz up the river

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: Jazz played up the river, as on a riverboat.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAD is traditional jazz; the Dart is a Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the New Orleans style revived in Britain.

clue.text: Slammed back hand

indicators.note: back tells us the word meaning hand over is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to hand something over is to deliver it

explanation.surface: A door was slammed back by a hand, or a tennis backhand was struck hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand' is a verb here, hand over, DELIVER, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam a play or person in criticism is to abuse and condemn them.

clue.text: Edited topic or line of columns

indicators.note: edited text is reworked, so the letters of the following two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor rewrites a subject or a line in newspaper columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'columns' suggests newspaper columns; it is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch whose roof rests on a row of pillars, as at the front of a classical building.

clue.text: Inner room, one with communal sleeping place in a holiday resort

parts.note: in a Scottish two-roomed cottage the ben is the inner room
I is the Roman numeral one
a dorm is a dormitory, a shared bedroom

explanation.surface: A holiday hotel where guests share an inner room and a dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN is a Scots word for the inner room of a cottage (the outer one is the but). BENIDORM is a Spanish resort popular with British package tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The town on Spain's Costa Blanca is a famous package-tour destination for sun and beaches.

clue.text: Stick heard to break by Eton's head

indicators.note: to break the word is to smash its letters and reassemble them
the head of the school's name is its first letter

explanation.surface: A schoolboy hears the Eton headmaster is to break a stick over him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' rearranges HEARD into ADHER, and 'head' of Eton gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain fastened, as glue does.
